# F4HWN v6.3.0

> [!NOTE]
> 🌐 Automatic translation is available through your browser or an online translation service.

# 🔥 About this firmware

This firmware is a fork of the [F4HWN custom firmware](https://github.com/armel/uv-k5-firmware-custom). It extends the work originally done for the UV-K5 V1 (DP32G030 MCU) and adapts it to the newer UV-K1 and UV-K5 V3, which are based on the PY32F071 MCU.

It is the result of joint work by [@muzkr](https://github.com/muzkr) and [@armel](https://github.com/armel). Many thanks to [@mrkusypl](https://github.com/mrkusypl), [@jdenoy](https://github.com/jdenoy), [@lemiller-dev](https://github.com/lemiller-dev), and everyone who tested, reported issues, contributed code, or supported the project.

Version 6.3.0 turns the experimental overlay platform into a much more capable radio-application environment. Overlay API v3 adds audio capture, precise timing, USB serial communication, application hand-off, safer transmission setup and display services, while Labs gains ten new applications ranging from AIS and marine DSC reception to KISS TNC, radiosonde decoders, CW USB and audio-analysis tools.

The four official editions remain available:

| Edition | Intended use | Additional features |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 Fusion | Everyday use | The balanced reference edition |
| 🧭 FieldOps | Field and first-responder operations | RescueOps controls, Fox Hunt and Morse Beacon |
| 📡 Transfer | Radio-to-radio data transfer | AirCopy and Beam wireless transfer |
| 🧪 Labs | Experimentation and early access | External-Flash overlay apps and experimental features |

For most users, Fusion remains the recommended edition.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Labs is experimental. It contains the newest and least-settled developments. Expect rough edges, changing behaviour and possible incompatibilities between versions.

> [!WARNING]
> THIS FIRMWARE HAS NO REAL BRAIN. PLEASE USE YOUR OWN.
>
> Use this firmware entirely at your own risk. There is absolutely no guarantee that it will work in any way, shape or form on your radio. It may even brick your radio, in which case you may need to buy another one.
>
> Anyway, have fun.

# ⚙️ Getting started

If you are already running Fusion Edition v5.x or v6.x, you can [flash](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/#flash) the v6.3.0 edition of your choice as usual.

Choose another edition only if you need its specific features:

- choose FieldOps for Fox Hunt, Morse Beacon and RescueOps controls;
- choose Transfer for AirCopy and Beam;
- choose Labs to use the experimental overlay-app platform.

If you are coming from a factory firmware or from a version earlier than Fusion Edition v5.x:

1. Optionally export your memory channels to CSV from CHIRP using the driver matching your currently installed firmware.
2. [Flash](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/#flash) the v6.3.0 edition of your choice.
3. Enter the hidden menus by holding `PTT + SIDE BUTTON 1️⃣` while powering on the radio, then release all keys and perform a `RESET ALL`.
4. Optionally reload your channels using the CHIRP driver matching v6.3.0.

> [!WARNING]
> Depending on the firmware you are upgrading from, changes to the memory and settings layout may require a complete reset.
>
> Export your channels and back up your calibration data before flashing.

> [!WARNING]
> When restoring channels from a CSV file, copy and paste them into a freshly downloaded radio image instead of importing the CSV file directly.

Remember to configure the navigation direction for your radio using the hidden `SetNav` menu:

- select the UV-K1 layout for the UV-K1;
- select the UV-K5 V3 layout for the UV-K5 V3.

# 🧩 Overlay API v3

Overlay API v3 is the foundation of this release. It keeps ABI major 1 and its append-only compatibility model, while providing applications with a much broader set of resident services:

- direct RX audio capture from PA4;
- a precise 48 MHz cycle clock for demodulators and timing-sensitive applications;
- resident integer formatters and frequency rendering;
- application-to-application hand-off with a bounded message payload;
- a quiet `tx_prepare` path for applications that control RF keying themselves;
- USB-C serial-port services, initially used by KISS TNC;
- page-level and byte-paced LCD output;
- K5Viewer updates separated from LCD writes, so time-critical receivers are not blocked by screen mirroring;
- deferred VFO changes applied safely when an application exits;
- more consistent API layout and capability reporting across firmware editions.

Existing applications that only require an earlier API level remain compatible with the append-only ABI. Applications that require API level 3 must be used with firmware v6.3.0 or later.

# 🆕 Ten new overlay applications

The Labs collection grows from 30 to 40 applications. New in this release:

- **AIS RX** — receives 9600-bit/s AIS traffic on AIS 1 or AIS 2 and decodes Class A, Class B, static, voyage and European Inland AIS reports. It displays vessel identity, position, speed, heading, destination and inland-navigation data. Real AIS reception has been validated.
- **ATIS DSC RX** — receives VHF Digital Selective Calling on marine channel 70 and displays distress, urgency, safety, routine and test calls, including MMSI, destination, distress nature, time and position. Bench-tested on radio; live channel-70 traffic remains to be validated.
- **KISS TNC** — turns the radio into a Bell 202 AFSK 1200 AX.25 TNC connected through USB-C. APRSdroid or another KISS client handles the map, messaging and beacon logic while the radio performs RF reception and transmission.
- **Sonde M10** — decodes Meteomodem M10 radiosondes and displays serial number, position, altitude, temperature, humidity, vertical speed, horizontal speed and heading. Live radiosonde reception has been validated.
- **Sonde RS41** — decodes classic and newer multi-GNSS Vaisala RS41 frames, displaying position, altitude, vertical and horizontal speed, heading and battery voltage. Classic RS41 reception has been validated in the field; multi-GNSS support is currently validated with synthetic frames.
- **CW USB** — a dedicated USB-C straight-key and paddle application derived from CW Keyer, with deliberate transmitter arming and selectable automatic, iambic A and iambic B modes. Thanks [@jdenoy](https://github.com/jdenoy) and [@lemiller-dev](https://github.com/lemiller-dev).
- **AF Scope** — an oscilloscope and audio-frequency tuner for the demodulated receiver output, with triggering, gain, persistence, peak detection, frequency measurement and known-tone comparison.
- **AF Spectro** — an audio spectrum and sonogram analyser with peak hold, two-tone detection and twist measurement for signals such as Bell 202 AFSK.
- **Resistor** — a 3-, 4-, 5- and 6-band resistor colour-code calculator with direct colour entry, tolerance and temperature-coefficient support.
- **Hell Maze** — a first-person fixed-point raycasting game with textured walls, enemies, sound effects and an on-screen help page.

AF Scope and AF Spectro can hand off directly to one another while preserving their shared audio-path settings.

> [!CAUTION]
> Receive-only applications do not make protected frequencies suitable for experimentation. Never transmit test signals on AIS channels, marine channel 70, operational radiosonde frequencies, paging networks, aeronautical channels or emergency-beacon bands.
>
> Transmitting applications must only be used on frequencies, power levels and modes permitted by your licence and local regulations.

# 📡 Existing application improvements

Existing applications also received substantial updates:

- **APRS TX and APRS Edit** now support a direct round trip: APRS TX opens the editor, the edited profile is committed, and the loader returns directly to TX. The profile also adds an `ARISS` path preset for the ISS digipeater.
- **POCSAG RX** now decodes 512 and 1200 baud simultaneously, identifies 2400-baud preambles, keeps up to ten pages and can optionally retain tone-only pages. `Tone Only` and `Text Lost` are now distinguished explicitly.
- **Sonde M20** adds GPS-derived vertical speed, horizontal speed and heading, relative humidity and an optional decode beep.
- **Sonde M10, M20 and RS41** now share a consistent telemetry layout and controls for frequency offset, attenuation and decode notification.
- **CW Decode** reaches v1.0 with crystal correction shared conceptually with CW Keyer, a reorganised display and more decoded-text space.
- **CW Keyer** has been separated from the new CW USB input variant. RF preparation, sidetone behaviour, timing, protection and receive display have also been refined.
- **SSTV** now uses page-level LCD updates during progressive reception, preventing K5Viewer traffic from blocking audio sampling. PTT is deliberately ignored; transmission starts only with `MENU`.
- **EPIRB 406** now plays a three-beep notification after a valid decode and returns to reception without the former amplifier click.
- **ATIS RX** uses slicer weights measured against the UV-K1 audio path, significantly improving decoding of realistic sine-FSK signals.
- **Beacon and Fox Hunt** add a silent-carrier lead-in to help receivers open their squelch, a callsign-only identification mode and idle intervals up to ten minutes. Existing saved settings are migrated.
- **Broadcast FM** now handles long key presses correctly.

# 🔌 KISS TNC and USB serial services

KISS TNC connects the radio to APRSdroid or any compatible KISS client through USB-C:

- received AX.25 frames with a valid FCS are forwarded to the host;
- host frames are transmitted using Bell 202 AFSK 1200;
- KISS data, `TXDELAY` and persistence commands are supported;
- channel-busy and half-duplex behaviour are handled by the application;
- an optional RX-only mode prevents host frames from being transmitted.

Reception and transmission have been validated with APRSdroid, including an on-air beacon received by an iGate.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> RF picked up by the USB cable can reset the USB connection during transmission. Use a short cable, keep the antenna away from the phone and cable, and fit a VHF-suitable clip-on ferrite at the radio end when necessary.

# 🔭 Audio-analysis tools

AF Scope and AF Spectro expose the demodulated audio path used by applications such as APRS RX, AIS RX, SSTV and the radiosonde decoders.

AF Scope provides:

- triggered oscilloscope views;
- automatic and manual gain;
- peak detection and persistence;
- steady-tone tuning and stability indication;
- single-tone and FSK frequency measurements.

AF Spectro provides:

- spectrum and scrolling sonogram views;
- peak hold and frequency-range tracking;
- dual-tone and DTMF inspection;
- Bell 202 twist measurement, useful when adjusting APRS transmit audio.

These tools analyse received audio after the BK4829 demodulator. They are not RF spectrum analysers and do not replace Spectrum3D.

# 🛠️ Reliability fixes

- Hardened overlay serial reads, writes, timeout recovery and USB link-state reporting.
- Prevented stale deferred-VFO state from leaking between application launches.
- Added runaway-chain protection for applications that repeatedly hand off to one another.
- Fixed CW Keyer's missing sidetone on the first keyed mark.
- Removed the click after EPIRB notification beeps and frequency changes.
- Fixed Broadcast FM long-press handling.
- Improved application cleanup of audio capture, serial ownership, staged hand-offs and display state.
- Kept time-critical LCD activity from interfering with SSTV and audio-analysis sampling.

# 📋 Changelog

## Added

- Added overlay API level 3 while preserving ABI major 1.
- Added resident audio capture, precise cycle timing, integer formatters and frequency drawing.
- Added application hand-off with bounded messages and runaway-chain protection.
- Added USB-C serial services for overlay applications.
- Added quiet TX preparation for applications that key the PA themselves.
- Added LCD page blits, paced LCD feeding and independent K5Viewer updates.
- Added deferred VFO staging on application exit.
- Added AIS RX and ATIS DSC RX.
- Added KISS TNC for APRSdroid and other KISS clients.
- Added Sonde M10 and Sonde RS41.
- Added CW USB.
- Added AF Scope and AF Spectro.
- Added the Resistor colour-code calculator.
- Added Hell Maze.
- Added APRS TX/Edit hand-off and the ARISS path preset.
- Added 512-baud reception and tone-only-page support to POCSAG RX.
- Added radiosonde velocity, humidity, battery and decode-notification fields where available.
- Added callsign-only identification and a silent-carrier lead-in to Beacon and Fox Hunt.

## Improved

- Increased the application collection from 30 to 40 installable applications.
- Improved ATIS RX decoding for the measured UV-K1 receive-audio response.
- Improved CW Decode display, crystal correction and tuning consistency.
- Improved CW Keyer RF preparation, sidetone, timing and protection behaviour.
- Improved POCSAG RX history from five to ten pages.
- Improved SSTV progressive rendering while K5Viewer is connected.
- Improved Sonde RS41 reception with edge lift and adaptive DPLL rate tracking.
- Added support for newer multi-GNSS RS41 position frames.
- Improved Sonde M10, M20 and RS41 display consistency.
- Extended Beacon and Fox Hunt idle intervals from four to ten minutes.
- Improved overlay serial-port error recovery and diagnostics.

## Fixed

- Fixed stale VFO staging after an overlay application exits.
- Fixed Broadcast FM long-press key handling.
- Fixed the first-mark sidetone in CW Keyer.
- Fixed the click after EPIRB notification beeps.
- Fixed potential K5Viewer blocking during progressive SSTV reception.
- Fixed USB serial timeout and unread-data handling when an application exits.
- Fixed several CW keying, arming and unwanted-transmission edge cases.
- Fixed application-chain loops returning indefinitely between overlays.

## Changed

- Bumped the firmware version to v6.3.0.
- Bumped the overlay API level from 2 to 3 while retaining ABI major 1.
- Split USB-C key and paddle input out of CW Keyer into the dedicated CW USB application.
- Changed SSTV transmission so that only `MENU`, never PTT, starts a transmission.
- Changed APRS TX profile editing to return directly from APRS Edit through application hand-off.
- Changed several decoder applications to use the resident audio-capture and timing services.
- Changed screen-intensive applications to use K5Viewer-safe LCD services.

# 📚 Wiki documentation

The project [Wiki](https://github.com/armel/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom/wiki) brings together the main documentation: getting started, CHIRP programming, UV Studio, radio operation, scanning, menu reference, button functions, advanced features, troubleshooting and videos.

Documentation for the experimental overlay applications is also available in their source directories.

# 🪛 Calibration data

[UV Studio](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/) can dump and restore calibration data. Keeping a separate backup for each radio is strongly recommended.

1. Open [Dump Calibration](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/#dump-calib).
2. Power on the radio in normal mode.
3. Click `Dump Calibration Data` and save the resulting `calibration.dat` file.
4. Rename the file with the serial number printed under the battery to avoid mixing backups from different radios.

# 🖥️ Live Viewer

UV Studio includes K5Viewer Live Viewer for screen mirroring, screenshots and remote keyboard control over USB or a compatible serial cable.

1. Keep the radio connected to your computer.
2. Open [UV Studio](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/).
3. Select Live Viewer, connect and choose the radio's serial port.

# 💾 CHIRP support

Use the CHIRP driver supplied with this release and matching firmware v6.3.0. It supports the UV-K1 and UV-K5 V3 editions and exposes the settings reported by the installed firmware.

Always use the CHIRP driver matching the firmware version installed on the radio.

# 📦 Release files

This release provides four firmware binaries:

- `f4hwn.fusion.v6.3.0.bin`
- `f4hwn.fieldops.v6.3.0.bin`
- `f4hwn.transfer.v6.3.0.bin`
- `f4hwn.labs.v6.3.0.bin`

It also includes:

- the CHIRP driver matching v6.3.0;
- the overlay applications compatible with API level 3.

For most users, install `f4hwn.fusion.v6.3.0.bin`.

# 📺 Presentation video

I also made a [presentation video](https://youtu.be/-9ZGm82OXbc) for this release, available on my YouTube channel.

# 🗃️ A larger overlay-app platform

The experimental Labs overlay platform now supports **48 application slots**, up from 16 in v6.1.0. Empty slots are hidden from the radio's app menu, so the list remains compact even when applications are spread across external Flash.

The app menu is also easier to use:

- holding `UP` or `DOWN` repeats navigation;
- `*` switches the right-hand column between app size and app version;
- the list refreshes when UV Studio installs or replaces an app;
- incompatible applications remain visible and report a clear error instead of disappearing silently.

The loader can now preserve an application's screen in external Flash when it exits. It also introduces a bounded configuration proxy, allowing a companion editor to update a versioned settings block owned by another installed app without moving application-specific logic into the resident firmware.

The external-Flash layout has been adjusted to make room for the expanded app area while preserving the Sonic 4K interoperability reserve. The RX/TX log has moved from `0x1E0000` to `0x018000`; existing v6.1.0 log entries are not migrated and the log therefore starts fresh after the update.

# 🆕 New overlay applications

The collection grows from 18 to 30 applications. New in this release:

- **Signal Finder** — direction finding for any carrier, with relative peak tracking, automatic attenuation and detection of the downward swept tone used by 121.5/243 MHz emergency homers. Thanks [@jdenoy](https://github.com/jdenoy).
- **CW Decode** — decodes A1A keyed carriers from the BK4829 RSSI envelope, with adaptive threshold, WPM tracking, AGC control and optional USB receive audio.
- **CW Keyer** — self-contained straight-key and paddle CW transmission with adjustable WPM, sidetone, receive pitch, semi-break-in delay and crystal correction.
- **ACARS RX** — experimental VHF ACARS receiver with parity and BCS checking, limited error repair and a three-message history. Bench-tested, but not yet validated with live aircraft traffic.
- **APRS DIGI** — a deliberately limited `WIDE1-1` / `WIDE2-1` fill-in digipeater with duplicate suppression, loop prevention and channel-busy protection.
- **APRS Edit** — edits the APRS TX callsign, SSID, position, path, symbol and comment of up to 64 characters through the new configuration proxy.
- **ATIS RX** — receives the ATIS identity burst used by European inland-waterway VHF radios and displays the station identity, call sign and country. Bench-tested; live boat traffic remains to be validated.
- **POCSAG RX** — receives 1200-baud pager traffic such as DAPNET, corrects one-bit BCH errors and keeps a five-page history. Bench-tested; live network reception remains to be validated.

# F4HWN v6.1.0

> [!NOTE]
> 🌐 Automatic translation is available through your browser or an online translation service.

# 🔥 About this firmware

This firmware is a fork of the [F4HWN custom firmware](https://github.com/armel/uv-k5-firmware-custom). It extends the work originally done for the UV-K5 V1 (DP32G030 MCU) and adapts it to the newer UV-K1 and UV-K5 V3, which are based on the PY32F071 MCU.

It is the result of joint work by [@muzkr](https://github.com/muzkr) and [@armel](https://github.com/armel). Many thanks to [@mrkusypl](https://github.com/mrkusypl), [@Sarijen](https://github.com/Sarijen), [@jdenoy](https://github.com/jdenoy), and everyone who tested, reported issues, contributed code, or supported the project.

Version 6.1.0 expands everyday monitoring in Fusion, makes multiboot configuration banks much faster to switch, and significantly extends the experimental overlay-app platform in Labs.

The four official editions remain available:

| Edition | Intended use | Additional features |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 Fusion | Everyday use | The balanced reference edition |
| 🧭 FieldOps | Field and first-responder operations | RescueOps controls, Fox Hunt and Morse Beacon |
| 📡 Transfer | Radio-to-radio data transfer | AirCopy and Beam wireless transfer |
| 🧪 Labs | Experimentation and early access | External-Flash overlay apps and experimental features |

For most users, Fusion remains the recommended edition.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Labs is experimental. It contains the newest and least-settled developments. Expect rough edges, changing behavior, and possible incompatibilities between versions.

> [!WARNING]
> THIS FIRMWARE HAS NO REAL BRAIN. PLEASE USE YOUR OWN.
>
> Use this firmware entirely at your own risk. There is absolutely no guarantee that it will work in any way, shape, or form on your radio. It may even brick your radio, in which case you may need to buy another one.
>
> Anyway, have fun.

# ⚙️ Getting started

If you are already running Fusion Edition v5.x, you can [flash](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/?firmwareURL=https://github.com/armel/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom/raw/main/archive/f4hwn.fusion.v6.1.0.bin#flash) the v6.1.0 edition of your choice as usual.

For most users, **Fusion Edition remains the recommended edition**.

Choose another edition only if you need its specific features:

- choose **FieldOps** for Fox Hunt, Morse Beacon and RescueOps controls;
- choose **Transfer** for AirCopy and Beam;
- choose **Labs** to test the experimental overlay-app platform.

A dedicated v6.1.0 CHIRP driver is provided as an attachment to these release notes. Make sure to use this driver with every v6.0.0 edition.

If you are coming from a factory firmware or from a version earlier than Fusion Edition v5.x, I recommend following these steps:

1. Optionally export your memory channels to CSV from CHIRP using the driver matching your currently installed firmware.
2. [Flash](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/?firmwareURL=https://github.com/armel/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom/raw/main/archive/f4hwn.fusion.v6.1.0.bin#flash) your UV-K1 or UV-K5 V3 with the v6.0.0 edition of your choice.
3. Enter the hidden menus by holding `PTT + SIDE BUTTON 1️⃣` while powering on the radio, then release all keys and perform a `RESET ALL`.
4. Optionally reload your channels using CHIRP with the dedicated v6.1.0 driver.

> [!WARNING]
> Depending on the firmware you are upgrading from, changes to the memory and settings layout may require a complete reset.
>
> Export your channels and back up your calibration data before flashing.

> [!WARNING]
> When restoring channels from a CSV file, copy and paste them into a freshly downloaded radio image instead of importing the CSV file directly.

Remember to configure the navigation direction for your radio using the hidden `SetNav` menu:

- select the UV-K1 layout for the UV-K1;
- select the UV-K5 V3 layout for the UV-K5 V3.

# 📺 Presentation video

I also made a [presentation video](https://youtu.be/ioNoV409Z3Q) for this release, available on my YouTube channel.

# 👀 Full Watch

Fusion v6.1.0 adds **Full Watch**, an extension of dual watch that can monitor:

- VFO A;
- VFO B;
- priority channel 1;
- priority channel 2.

The `RxMode` menu now provides two additional modes:

- `FULL RX / RESPOND` monitors all configured channels and replies on the channel that opened the squelch;
- `MAIN TX / FULL RX` monitors all configured channels but always transmits on the selected main VFO.

Priority channels use the existing scan-list priority settings. Duplicate or unavailable priority channels are ignored automatically. Animated chevrons show the background watch cycle, and channel navigation now returns cleanly from a temporary priority-channel display.

# 🔄 Instant configuration-bank switching

The `SetCfg` menu can now apply another multiboot configuration bank immediately, without restarting the radio or restoring another firmware slot.

Changing banks reloads the complete operating state, including channels, VFOs, scan lists, menu settings, display configuration, and edition-specific settings. The status bar displays the active bank as `CFG M` or `CFG 1` to `CFG 4`, so the selected configuration remains visible during normal use.

Each firmware slot may therefore use its matching bank, share a bank with another slot, or switch between several independent operating configurations while the same firmware remains active.

# 📋 Mixed scan lists

The scan-list selector now includes a `MIX` mode. It lets you choose any combination of the available scan lists and scan them as one set.

The menu displays the number of selected lists, making large channel plans easier to check before starting a scan.

# 🗃️ Overlay applications

The experimental Labs overlay platform has received its largest update so far.

The number of external-Flash app slots has increased from 8 to 16. Overlay API v2 adds read-only assets, allowing fonts, text, bitmaps, tables, and other static resources to remain in external Flash instead of consuming the 4 KiB executable overlay. App settings are preserved when an app is updated, and the firmware now reports code and asset sizes separately.

New applications include:

- **APRS RX** — receives Bell 202 AFSK 1200 AX.25 UI frames, decodes common position formats and Mic-E, displays APRS symbols and RSSI, and keeps a five-frame history;
- **APRS TX** — edits and transmits APRS beacons with callsign, SSID, path, symbol, and position;
- **SSTV** — receives 14 SSTV modes and can transmit the radio's boot logo, including Robot, Martin, Scottie, and PD modes used by ARISS events;
- **EPIRB 406** — receives and decodes first-generation 406 MHz emergency-beacon messages, including beacon ID, country, protocol, position, and BCH status;
- **SysInfo** — displays detailed firmware, memory, external-Flash, multiboot, and runtime diagnostics;
- **Spectrum3D** — renders a fast scrolling 3D spectrum waterfall;
- **Minesweeper** — a complete minesweeper game with title screen and persistent settings;
- **Snake** — the classic snake game;
- **Space Impact** — a side-scrolling arcade game;
- **Rapid Roll** — a platform arcade game.

Existing apps also received substantial improvements. Cube3D now offers more shapes, zoom, speed, pause, and wire/solid rendering controls. Plasma, Breakout, Beam, and the shared app runtime use less Flash and RAM.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Overlay apps are intended for the Labs edition. An app must match the overlay ABI and capabilities provided by the installed firmware. Apps built for v6.0.0 may be rejected when they depend on retired services; install the v6.1.0 app files supplied with this release.

> [!CAUTION]
> APRS TX, SSTV TX, EPIRB, Beacon, and other transmitting apps must only be used on frequencies, power levels, and modes permitted by your licence and local regulations. Never transmit test signals in the protected 406.0–406.1 MHz distress-beacon band.

# 🚀 AirCopy and external-Flash tools

The Transfer edition's AirCopy implementation is faster and more capable:

- multi-block FSK framing approximately doubles transfer speed;
- blocks that are already identical are skipped;
- TX and RX selections are validated more strictly;
- UART-assisted transfer and complete external-Flash cloning are supported.

Labs also adds external-Flash dump and restore through UV Studio, with CRC32 verification. The radio's device-specific calibration sector remains protected during restore operations.

https://api.github.com/repos/armel/uv-k1.body: > 🌐 **Translate** > Automatic translation is available via Google Translate: [Open translated version](https://translate.google.com/translate?sl=auto&tl=fr&u=https://github.com/armel/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom/releases/tag/v6.0.0). # 🔥 About this firmware This firmware is a fork of the [F4HWN custom firmware](https://github.com/armel/uv-k5-firmware-custom). It extends the work originally done for the UV-K5 V1 (DP32G030 MCU) and adapts it to the newer UV-K1 and UV-K5 V3, which are based on the PY32F071 MCU. It is the result of joint work by [@muzkr](https://github.com/muzkr) and [@armel](https://github.com/armel). Many thanks to [@mrkusypl](https://github.com/mrkusypl) for his huge contributions! Version 6.0.0 marks an important evolution of the project. Fusion is no longer the only official edition. The firmware is now available in four editions, all sharing the same core but targeting different uses: | Edition | Intended use | Additional features | |---|---|---| | 🔥 **Fusion** | Everyday use | The balanced reference edition | | 🧭 **FieldOps** | Field and first-responder operations | RescueOps controls, Fox Hunt and Morse Beacon | | 📡 **Transfer** | Radio-to-radio data transfer | AirCopy and Beam wireless transfer | | 🧪 **Labs** | Experimentation and early access | External-Flash overlay apps and experimental features | Each edition displays its own name in the welcome and system-information screens. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Labs is experimental.** > > It includes the newest and least-settled developments. Expect rough edges, changing behavior and possible incompatibilities between versions. > > Labs is not necessarily a strict superset of all the other editions. Some features may be exchanged between releases to preserve stability, RAM and Flash headroom. > [!WARNING] > **THIS FIRMWARE HAS NO REAL BRAIN. PLEASE USE YOUR OWN.** > > Use this firmware entirely at your own risk. There is absolutely no guarantee that it will work in any way, shape or form on your radio. It may even brick your radio, in which case you may need to buy another one. > > Anyway, have fun. # ⚙️ Getting started If you are already running Fusion Edition v5.x, you can [flash](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/?firmwareURL=https://github.com/armel/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom/raw/main/archive/f4hwn.fusion.v6.0.0.bin#flash) the v6.0.0 edition of your choice as usual. For most users, **Fusion Edition remains the recommended edition**. Choose another edition only if you need its specific features: - choose **FieldOps** for Fox Hunt, Morse Beacon and RescueOps controls; - choose **Transfer** for AirCopy and Beam; - choose **Labs** to test the experimental overlay-app platform. A dedicated v6.0.0 CHIRP driver is provided as an attachment to these release notes. Make sure to use this driver with every v6.0.0 edition. If you are coming from a factory firmware or from a version earlier than Fusion Edition v5.x, I recommend following these steps: 1. Optionally export your memory channels to CSV from CHIRP using the driver matching your currently installed firmware. 2. [Flash](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/?firmwareURL=https://github.com/armel/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom/raw/main/archive/f4hwn.fusion.v6.0.0.bin#flash) your UV-K1 or UV-K5 V3 with the v6.0.0 edition of your choice. 3. Enter the hidden menus by holding `PTT + SIDE BUTTON 1️⃣` while powering on the radio, then release all keys and perform a `RESET ALL`. 4. Optionally reload your channels using CHIRP with the dedicated v6.0.0 driver. > [!WARNING] > Depending on the firmware you are upgrading from, changes to the memory and settings layout may require a complete reset. > > Export your channels and back up your calibration data before flashing. > [!WARNING] > When restoring channels from a CSV file, copy and paste them into a freshly downloaded radio image instead of importing the CSV file directly. Remember to configure the navigation direction for your radio using the hidden `SetNav` menu: - select the UV-K1 layout for the UV-K1; - select the UV-K5 V3 layout for the UV-K5 V3. # 📺 Presentation video I also made a presentation [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_iWIly3-mO0) for this release, available on my YouTube channel: # 🧩 The four editions Version 6.0.0 is now available in four editions, each designed for a different use case. ## 🔥 Fusion Fusion remains the reference edition and the recommended choice for most users. Compared with Fusion v5.9.0, it no longer includes: - AirCopy and Beam; - RescueOps; - Fox Hunt and Beacon; - Breakout. These features remain available in the specialized editions below. ## 🧭 FieldOps FieldOps includes the Fusion feature set, plus: - RescueOps; - Fox Hunt and Beacon. ## 📡 Transfer Transfer includes the Fusion feature set, plus: - AirCopy and Beam. ## 🧪 Labs Labs is the experimental edition. It includes: - the Fusion feature set; - RescueOps; - AirCopy; - the external-Flash overlay-app platform. The first available overlay apps include: - Broadcast FM; - Fox Hunt; - Beacon; - Beam; - Breakout; - Tetris; - Cube3D; - Plasma. > [!IMPORTANT] > Labs contains the newest and least-settled developments. Expect rough edges, changing behavior and possible incompatibilities between releases. > > Labs is not a strict superset of Fusion, FieldOps and Transfer. Its feature set may evolve depending on stability and available memory. # 🚀 Multiboot Version 6.0.0 introduces a new multiboot architecture using the radio's external Flash memory. It provides: - one automatically maintained **Main** firmware backup; - four additional firmware slots; - firmware edition and version display for each valid slot; - integrity validation before restoring a slot; - confirmation and progress screens; - protection against incomplete or corrupted firmware images; - a dedicated configuration bank for each slot; - the ability to select a configuration bank independently through `SetCfg`; - automatic restoration of the selected firmware into internal Flash. To open the multiboot selector: 1. power off the radio; 2. hold `MENU`; 3. power on the radio; 4. release the key when the multiboot screen appears. Use `UP` and `DOWN` to select a firmware, `MENU` to restore it and `EXIT` to return without making changes. > [!CAUTION] > Never power off the radio while a firmware slot is being restored. The firmware initially flashed through the normal bootloader is automatically preserved as **Main**. It can later be restored from the multiboot selector. Each multiboot slot normally uses its own memory channels and settings bank, allowing different editions or configurations to coexist without overwriting one another. # 🛠️ Multiconfig Each firmware stored in the multiboot system can use its own independent configuration bank. A configuration bank contains: - memory channels and their names; - VFO settings; - scan lists; - radio settings; - edition-specific settings. By default, each firmware slot is associated with the configuration bank bearing the same number. Switching to another multiboot slot therefore also restores the corresponding channels and settings. The new `SetCfg` menu makes it possible to select a different configuration bank without changing the firmware edition currently running. This allows, for example, the same firmware edition to be used with several completely different configurations, or multiple editions to share the same channels and settings when their capabilities are compatible. > [!IMPORTANT] > Some settings are only available in specific editions. When sharing a configuration bank between editions, unsupported settings are ignored and preserved whenever possible. # 🗃️ Overlay applications The 🧪 Labs edition introduces a new overlay-application platform. Unlike regular firmware features, overlay applications are not permanently stored in the MCU's internal Flash. They are stored in the radio's external Flash memory and copied into a dedicated 4 KiB RAM area only when launched. This makes it possible to add applications without permanently consuming the limited internal Flash space required by the main firmware. Installed applications are available from the `Apps` selector. Each application is validated before execution, and incompatible or corrupted application files are rejected. The first available overlay applications are: - **Beam** — wireless channel transfer between compatible radios; - **Broadcast FM** — FM broadcast receiver; - **Fox Hunt** — signal-hunting receiver; - **Beacon** — Morse beacon transmitter; - **Breakout** — arcade game; - **Tetris** — falling-block puzzle game; - **Cube3D** — real-time rotating 3D cube; - **Plasma** — full-screen demoscene effect. > [!WARNING] > Overlay applications are currently experimental and intended for the Labs edition. > > An application must be compatible with the overlay ABI and capabilities provided by the installed firmware. An application built for another firmware version or memory layout may be rejected. # 📋 Changelog ## Added - Added four official editions: **Fusion**, **FieldOps**, **Transfer** and **Labs**. - Added the multiboot platform with one automatic Main backup and four user firmware slots. - Added separate memory and settings banks for multiboot slots. - Added the `SetCfg` menu to select a configuration bank independently of the running firmware slot. - Added firmware edition, version and slot information to the multiboot and system-information screens. - Added the external-Flash overlay-app platform to Labs. - Added a versioned overlay-app ABI with capability discovery. - Added the Apps selector for discovering and launching installed overlay apps. - Added the Tetris overlay app. - Added the Cube3D overlay app. - Added the Plasma overlay app. - Added overlay versions of Beam, Broadcast FM, Fox Hunt, Beacon and Breakout. - Added K5Viewer support to the multiboot selector and overlay apps. - Added complete memory and settings transfer through AirCopy. - Added an optional `CARR` carrier-keying mode to Morse Beacon. - Added a no-heap build option to reclaim unused RAM. ## Improved - Improved AirCopy reliability with acknowledgement and automatic resend handling. - Improved AirCopy progress and error reporting. - Improved Beam channel transfers and channel-field handling. - Improved Beam VFO restoration and deferred channel saving. - Improved the multiboot interface, slot validation, restore progress and recovery behavior. - Improved multiboot safety when encountering incomplete, corrupted or uncertain external-Flash state. - Improved preservation of settings when switching between editions. - Improved the Apps selector and overlay-app user interface. - Improved memory usage shared by multiboot and overlay apps. - Improved Broadcast FM display and Flash usage. - Improved Fox Hunt, Breakout and Tetris Flash and RAM usage. - Improved overlay-app backlight behavior using the configured `BLTime`. - Improved overlay-app shortcuts and audio-service sharing. - Improved K5Viewer and serial-session behavior. - Improved the `F` status indicator. - Improved compatibility of the build scripts with macOS Bash 3.2. ## Fixed - Fixed a CHIRP upload stall when the final EEPROM write block was not aligned. - Fixed oversized EEPROM read commands that could expose memory outside the expected buffer. Thanks [@BB-KING777](https://github.com/BB-KING777). - Strengthened serial-command input validation to prevent unintended memory disclosure. - Fixed AirCopy transfers being interrupted or silently corrupted by lost packets. - Fixed Broadcast FM starting while a VFO was already receiving. - Fixed Broadcast FM scans being interrupted by reception on the main radio channel. - Fixed Beam failing to restore the previous VFO state in some situations. - Fixed Beacon carrier keying remaining disabled after switching from `CARR` to `TONE` during an idle window. - Fixed the backlight timer not being re-armed by key presses inside overlay apps. - Fixed the backlight being forced off when a serial session was initialized. - Fixed optional UART and USB build configurations. - Fixed RescueOps settings not always being preserved across editions. - Fixed side-key actions referring to features unavailable in the current edition. - Fixed scan-list name timing being counted at the wrong scheduler rate. - Fixed several multiboot state, configuration-bank and low-RAM edge cases. ## Changed - Split the former single Fusion distribution into four purpose-oriented editions. - Renamed the former Field preset to **FieldOps**. - Decoupled Fox Hunt and Beacon so that each feature can be included independently. - Moved experimental and memory-intensive features to the Labs overlay-app platform. - Stabilized action identifiers across editions. - Replaced firmware build-option reporting with CHIRP capability reporting. - Removed the legacy AM Fix implementation and its related settings. - Removed obsolete build options and unused reserved heap space. - Renamed `compile-with-docker.sh` to `compile-firmware.sh`; the old command remains available as a compatibility wrapper. - Added `compile-app.sh` for building overlay applications. # 📚 Wiki documentation To complement these release notes, remember that a GitHub [Wiki](https://github.com/armel/uv-k1-k5v3-firmware-custom/wiki) is available. It brings together the main documentation in one place: getting started, programming with CHIRP, using UV Studio, radio operation, scanning, menu reference, button functions, advanced features, troubleshooting, and videos/tutorials. The documentation will progressively be updated to cover the four editions, multiboot and the Labs overlay-app platform. # 🪛 Dumping and restoring calibration data [UV Studio](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/) can dump and restore calibration data, which is strongly recommended. Ideally, you should: - create a calibration dump immediately after installing the F4HWN firmware; - keep one backup for each radio you own; - restore it before installing different firmware, for example when returning to the stock firmware. ## Dump 1. Open [UV Studio](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/). 2. Power on your radio in normal mode. 3. Click **Dump Calibration Data**. 4. Select the radio's serial port when prompted. 5. Download and safely store the resulting `calibration.dat` file. > [!NOTE] > A good practice is to rename the calibration file using the serial number printed on the label under the battery. This prevents calibration files from being mixed up if you own multiple radios. ## Restore 1. Open [UV Studio](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/). 2. Power on your radio in normal mode. 3. Select your `calibration.dat` file. 4. Click **Restore Calibration Data**. 5. Select the radio's serial port and wait until the operation is fully complete. # 🖥️ About the Live Viewer feature [UV Studio](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/) includes the K5Viewer Live Viewer. It can be used on a computer with a Chromium-based browser such as Chrome, Edge, Brave or Opera, as well as Firefox 151 or later. Quick start: 1. Flash your Quansheng UV-K1 or UV-K5 V3 with one of the compatible F4HWN v6.0.0 editions. 2. Keep the radio connected to your computer using a compatible USB serial cable or its USB-C connection. 3. Open [UV Studio Live Viewer](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/#live). 4. Click **Connect** and select the radio's serial port. That's it. Nothing to install. Nothing to configure. Just plug and view 🤭 # 💾 CHIRP support A dedicated v6.0.0 CHIRP driver supporting the UV-K1 and UV-K5 V3 is provided as an attachment to these release notes. It supports the four editions and allows reading and writing memory channels, settings and basic parameters directly from CHIRP. The driver also uses firmware capability information to expose only the settings supported by the currently installed edition. This driver is provided for convenience and early testing. It may still evolve as feedback comes in, so feel free to open an issue or report any anomaly you notice. # 📦 Release files This release provides four firmware binaries: - `f4hwn.fusion.bin` - `f4hwn.fieldops.bin` - `f4hwn.transfer.bin` - `f4hwn.labs.bin` The release also includes: - the dedicated v6.0.0 CHIRP driver; - the overlay-app files intended for Labs; For most users, install `f4hwn.fusion.bin`. # ⚙️ Build summary ### Flash (limit: 120832 B / 118.00 KiB) | Preset | Used (B) | Used (KiB) | Free (B) | Free (KiB) | Usage | |----------|---------:|-----------:|---------:|-----------:|------:| | Fusion | 106892 | 104.39 | 13940 | 13.61 | 88.46% | | Transfer | 111284 | 108.68 | 9548 | 9.32 | 92.10% | | FieldOps | 113020 | 110.37 | 7812 | 7.63 | 93.53% | | Labs | 111908 | 109.29 | 8924 | 8.71 | 92.61% | ### RAM (limit: 16384 B / 16.00 KiB) | Preset | Used (B) | Used (KiB) | Free (B) | Free (KiB) | Usage | |----------|---------:|-----------:|---------:|-----------:|------:| | Fusion | 11968 | 11.69 | 4416 | 4.31 | 73.05% | | Transfer | 12128 | 11.84 | 4256 | 4.16 | 74.02% | | FieldOps | 12192 | 11.91 | 4192 | 4.09 | 74.41% | | Labs | 12224 | 11.94 | 4160 | 4.06 | 74.61% | Enjoy, Armel, F4HWN

Improved Beacon safety by enforcing function lock, TX lock, battery voltage, and modulation restrictions before every transmission (issue #478). - Improved Beacon operation for ARDF use: - changed the Morse speed to approximately 12 WPM, - repeated the selected identifier for the complete TX window, - added support for classic five-fox timing with an idle interval of up to four minutes. - Improved Beacon controls with a consistent layout: - Improved RAM usage by moving read-only lookup tables to Flash. - Improved Fox Hunt code size by: - sharing common display and interpolation helpers, - reducing temporary and persistent buffer sizes, - calculating PGA attenuation directly instead of using a lookup table, - removing per-column modulo operations from the signal-history renderer, - avoiding unnecessary Beacon message construction. - Reduced Fox Hunt Flash usage by a further 52 bytes through targeted refactoring and hot-path optimization. - Fixed RX mode restoration after leaving Close Call (issue #478). - Fixed RX mode restoration when switching from an active channel or frequency scan to Broadcast FM, Close Call, or CTCSS/DCS scanning (issue #480). - Fixed restart handling in modal applications, including Air Copy, Breakout, Frequency Scanner, Spectrum Analyzer, UART, and Fox Hunt. - Fixed restart commands being lost during an active Beacon TX window by servicing maintenance commands between CW characters. - Fixed Beacon transmissions bypassing normal TX safety restrictions. - Fixed progressive Beacon text positioning for callsign and fox identifiers. - Fixed K5Viewer keepalive handling during long Beacon TX windows. - Fixed Fox Hunt settings being lost when the radio powers off without leaving the application normally. ## Maintenance - Added the `ENABLE_FEAT_F4HWN_FOXHUNT` feature flag and enabled it for Fusion. - Extended the persisted Fox Hunt configuration from five to seven bytes to include the selected fox identifier and TX window. - Extended the VFO compatibility mapping so AirCopy includes all persisted Fox Hunt and Beacon settings. - Flash your Quansheng UV-K1 or UV-K5 V3 with the F4HWN 🔥 Fusion edition. 2. Keep the radio connected to your computer using a compatible USB serial cable or its USB-C connection. 3. Open the [UV Studio Live Viewer](https://armel.github.io/uvstudio/#live). 4. Click **Connect** and select the radio’s serial port. That’s it. Nothing to install. Nothing to configure. Just plug and view 🤭 # 💾 CHIRP Support A CHIRP [f4hwn.fusion.chirp.v5.8.0.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30710663/f4hwn.fusion.chirp.v5.8.0.py) driver supporting the UV-K1 and UV-K5 V3 is also included in this release. It works on desktop versions of Chrome, Chromium and Edge, and does not require installing any additional driver or software on your computer.

There are **two separate builds**: one for the UV-K1 and one for the UV-K5 V3. The reason is simple: these two radios use different navigation controls (left/right on the UV-K1, up/down on the UV-K5 V3), which directly affects how you move through menus and access options.

- create a calibration dump right after installing the F4HWN firmware, and  
- restore it before installing a different firmware (for example, when returning to the stock firmware).

- Power on your radio in **normal mode**.
- Click **Dump Calibration Data**.

> [!NOTE]
> A good practice is to rename your calibration file using the serial number of your radio, which is printed on the label on the back of the device (under the battery). This avoids mixing up calibration files if you own multiple units.

- Click **Restore Calibration Data** and wait until the process fully completes.

2️⃣ Keep the K5 connected to your PC via the USB cable (⚠️ Baofeng/Kenwood like USB serial cable only, not USB C)
3️⃣ Go to [https://armel.github.io/k5viewer/](https://armel.github.io/k5viewer/)
4️⃣ Click Connect (and select the serial port)

That’s it. Nothing to install. Nothing to configure. Just plug and view 🤭

# CHIRP Support

A CHIRP driver supporting the UV-K1 and UV-K5 V3 is also included in this release (see the attached file).
It allows reading and writing the radio’s memory channels, settings and basic parameters directly from CHIRP, just like with the UV-K5 V1.

This driver is provided for convenience and early testing.
It may still evolve as feedback comes in, so feel free to open an issue or report any anomaly you notice.

Enjoy,

Armel F4HWN

## Warning! New but incompatible hardware versions sold!
- This release is compatible with UV-K5/6 hardware version 3 and UV-K1 **ONLY**!
- **Check carefully which hardware version do you have before flashing any firmware!**
- **Do NOT flash this firmware on version 1 or version 2!**
- Do NOT use k5prog, k5prog-win or old webflasher to flash this firmware!

![uvk5_v3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d83bc1f-6241-429f-95ca-3adeb4057245)

### Changes
- Fox distance prediction for ARDF
- ARDF mode: Use negative gain indexes to get additional attenuation by
  * Disabling input LNA and 15dB gain (gain index -1)
  * Disabling input LNA with no gain (gain index -2)
  * Tuning to second harmonic (gain index -3)
  * Tuning to third harmonic (gain index -4)

- **Check carefully which hardware version do you have before flashing any firmware!**
- **Do NOT flash this firmware on version 1 or version 2!**
- Do NOT use k5prog, k5prog-win or old webflasher to flash this firmware!
- For UV-K5V3 and UV-K1 firmware flashing only use UVTOOLS2 [1]

- rework manual gain table
